repositories.description: Voice-to-text dictation app with local (Nvidia Parakeet/Whisper) and cloud models (BYOK). Privacy-first and available cross-platform.
repositories.readme:
OpenWhispr

The open-source and free alternative to WisprFlow and Granola.
Privacy-first voice-to-text dictation with AI agents, meeting transcription, and notes. Cross-platform for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Website · Docs · Download · API · Changelog

--- OpenWhispr turns your voice into text, notes, and actions from your desktop. Press a hotkey, speak, and your words appear at your cursor. Choose between fully private offline transcription with local speech-to-text models like Orukeet, Whisper, NVIDIA Parakeet, and Cohere Transcribe — where your audio never leaves your device — or cloud processing for speed. No data collection, no telemetry, fully open source. ## Download | Platform | Download | | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | [`.dmg`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | | macOS (Intel) \* | [`.dmg`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | | Windows | [`.exe`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | | Linux | [`.AppImage`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) / [`.deb`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) / [`.rpm`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) / [`.tar.gz`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | \* On Intel Macs, live speaker identification and voice fingerprinting are unavailable: they depend on ONNX Runtime, which [stopped shipping macOS x86_64 binaries in 1.24](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/tag/v1.24.1). Meetings still record and transcribe normally, and notes search falls back to keyword matching instead of semantic search. On macOS or x86_64 Linux, you can also install the community-maintained [Homebrew cask](https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/openwhispr): ```bash brew install --cask openwhispr ``` ## Features - **Voice dictation** — global hotkey to dictate into any app with automatic pasting - **Dictation translation** — dedicated hotkey to dictate in one language and paste the text in another - **AI agent** — talk to GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, Groq, Tinfoil, OpenRouter, or local models with a named voice assistant - **Voice Assistant hotkey** — dedicated hotkey that sends what you say straight to your AI assistant as a command, no wake word needed and no cleanup pass; highlighted text is edited in place. With auto-paste enabled, answers paste at a focused text cursor or stream into a floating panel and copy to the clipboard when no writable cursor is available. You can also opt in to sending a screenshot of your current screen as context - **Meeting transcription** — auto-detect Zoom, Teams, and FaceTime calls with live speaker diarization, voice fingerprinting, and Google, Microsoft, or Apple Calendar integration - **Local speaker diarization** — on-device speaker labelling with voice fingerprint recognition across meetings, no cloud required - **Notes** — create, organize, and search notes with folders, semantic search, cloud sync, and AI actions - **Team spaces & sharing** — free for signed-in users; share notes on the web with link, domain, or invite-only visibility, and collaborate in team spaces with roles, invitations, and server-enforced membership - **Audio import** — transcribe existing audio and video: drag in files, batch-upload, or paste a YouTube/audio URL, with optional speaker detection - **Local or cloud — your choice** — all core features (transcription, AI reasoning, speaker diarization, semantic search) work with local models or cloud providers — including GPU-accelerated local Whisper on Metal, CUDA, and Vulkan (AMD/Intel) - **Enterprise controls** — enforce organization policy, company SSO and SCIM, and centrally managed Amazon Bedrock or Azure OpenAI access without distributing cloud keys - **Public API & MCP** — manage notes and transcriptions programmatically or connect your AI assistant via the [MCP server](https://docs.openwhispr.com/integrations/mcp) ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr.git cd openwhispr npm install npm run dev ``` Requires Node.js 24+. See the [full documentation](https://docs.openwhispr.com/quickstart) for setup guides, platform-specific instructions, and build details. The commands above run the desktop application, which remains at the repository root. The Expo mobile application lives in [`openwhispr-mobile`](openwhispr-mobile/) with its own dependencies, lockfile, build configuration, and release process. See the [mobile README](openwhispr-mobile/README.md) for its setup instructions. ## Documentation Visit **[docs.openwhispr.com](https://docs.openwhispr.com)** for: - [Getting started](https://docs.openwhispr.com/quickstart) - [Platform guides](https://docs.openwhispr.com/platform/macos) (macOS, Windows, Linux) - [API reference](https://docs.openwhispr.com/api/overview) - [MCP server setup](https://docs.openwhispr.com/integrations/mcp) - [Troubleshooting](https://docs.openwhispr.com/troubleshooting) Repo examples: - [Custom ASR shim](examples/custom-asr-shim/) for Self-Hosted transcription against non-OpenAI-compatible ASR APIs ## Tech stack React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Electron 41, better-sqlite3, whisper.cpp, sherpa-onnx, shadcn/ui ## Star History [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=OpenWhispr/openwhispr&type=date&legend=top-left)](https://www.star-history.com/#OpenWhispr/openwhispr&type=date&legend=top-left) ## Sponsors

Neon is the serverless Postgres platform powering OpenWhispr Cloud.

## Contributing We welcome contributions. Fork the repo, create a feature branch, and open a pull request. See the [contributing guide](https://docs.openwhispr.com/contributing) for development setup and guidelines. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) — free for personal and commercial use. ## Acknowledgments - **[OpenAI Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper)** — speech recognition model powering local and cloud transcription - **[whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp)** — high-performance C++ implementation for local processing - **[NVIDIA Parakeet](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3)** — fast multilingual ASR model - **[sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx)** — cross-platform ONNX runtime for Parakeet inference - **[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/)** — model hub hosting Whisper, Parakeet, and embedding model weights - **[llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp)** — local LLM inference for AI text processing - **[Electron](https://www.electronjs.org/)** — cross-platform desktop framework - **[React](https://react.dev/)** — UI component library - **[shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/)** — accessible components built on Radix primitives - **[Neon](https://console.neon.tech/app/?promo=openwhispr)** — serverless Postgres powering OpenWhispr Cloud

repositories.name: context-mode
repositories.description: Free, local plugin that keeps tool output out of your coding agent's context window. Sandbox and SQLite FTS5 search, 99% fewer bytes in context. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and 4 more agents. Zero telemetry.
repositories.readme:
# Context Mode **A free, local plugin for 10 coding agents. It keeps tool output out of your agent's context window and keeps all usage data on your machine. The plugin is free forever.** [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/context-mode?label=npm%20downloads)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/context-mode) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/mksglu/context-mode?style=flat&color=yellow)](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1478479412700909750?label=Discord&logo=discord&color=5865f2)](https://discord.gg/DCN9jUgN5v) [![License: ELv2](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-ELv2-blue.svg)](LICENSE) **33K GitHub stars · 683K npm downloads** (read 2026-11-01, [stats.json](stats.json)) · on the Hacker News front page and GitHub Trending: [charts and sources](#adoption-stars-and-npm-downloads) > The Context Mode plugin is free and local, with its source open on GitHub. **Context Mode Gateway** is a separate hosted service with its own account and subscription. It takes the same idea from tool output to the whole conversation: Gateway Recall keeps long sessions searchable, and Gateway Memory shares what your agents learn across sessions and tools. [See how the Gateway works](https://contextmode.ai/docs/how-saving-works?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=quote) **Contents:** [Why](#why) · [Adoption](#adoption-stars-and-npm-downloads) · [Install](#install) · [Try it](#try-it) · [Use cases](#use-cases) · [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Tools](#tools) · [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) · [Context Mode Gateway](#context-mode-gateway) · [License](#license) · [Community](#community) ## Why A coding agent reads files, runs commands and fetches pages, and every result goes into its context window. The Context Mode plugin runs that work in a local sandbox, keeps the full output in a SQLite index on your machine, and gives the agent the part it asks for. - **The plugin is free forever.** Use it at home and at work, free of charge, under a source-available license. - **Runs on your machine.** The hooks, the sandbox and search run as local processes next to your agent. - **The plugin keeps your data on your machine.** Every index lives in `~/.context-mode`: one `context.db` per project. - **Zero telemetry.** The plugin keeps all usage data on your machine. [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) lists each network call it makes. - **Works offline after install.** Sandbox runs, file indexing and search use local SQLite and your own runtimes. - **Thinking in Code.** The agent writes a short script instead of reading the data, and only what the script prints reaches the context: see [How it works, step 5](#thinking-in-code). - **Small replies.** On the 36 bench rows with 10 KB or more of raw output, the plugin's median reply is 99.4% smaller than the raw output. ## Adoption: stars and npm downloads
Open the [interactive chart](https://contextmode.ai/open-source/stats?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=adoption#daily) and point at a bar to read its value. Tabs there show days, weeks, months and years. Stars come from the GitHub GraphQL API (`starredAt`); npm downloads come from `api.npmjs.org/downloads/range`. The total up to 2026-10-29 is 683K npm downloads (`stats.json` keeps a daily copy). A daily job redraws both charts. - **Hacker News.** "MCP server that reduces Claude Code context consumption by 98%" reached the front page with 570+ points and 107 comments on 2026-02-28 ([thread](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47193064)). - **GitHub Trending.** A bot that watches GitHub Trending logged the repo there on 14 days from 2026-04-24 to 2026-10-17 ([uibm/trending-watcher](https://github.com/uibm/trending-watcher/issues?q=%22mksglu%2Fcontext-mode%22)). Starred by engineers at these companies: each name is the company field of 2 or more stargazer profiles, read with the GitHub GraphQL API on 2026-11-01 ([data](docs/assets/readme/data/stargazer-companies.json)). ## Install Pick your agent: [Claude Code](#install-claude-code) · [Codex](#install-codex) · [Gemini CLI](#install-gemini) · [Qwen Code](#install-qwen) · [Pi](#install-pi) · [OpenCode](#install-opencode) · [Copilot CLI](#install-copilot-cli) · [Kiro](#install-kiro) · [VS Code](#install-vscode) · [ZCode](#install-zcode) Open its block and copy its own install command. Each block also holds the update, check and remove steps, and the [Install guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/install?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install) walks through them. The plugin needs Node 24.15.0 or later, from the engines field in [package.json](package.json). On Windows, add Git for Windows: the shell tools run in Git Bash, and doctor checks for it. contextmode installs as the npm package and command `context-mode`. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code install from GitHub, and each of their commands names the release branch.
Claude Code ```sh claude plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode claude plugin install context-mode@context-mode ``` ```sh # update claude plugin update context-mode@context-mode # check claude plugin list # remove claude plugin marketplace remove context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (package) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
Codex ```sh codex plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode codex plugin add context-mode@context-mode # one-time step: trust the plugin hooks npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup --agents codex ``` ```sh # update codex plugin marketplace upgrade context-mode # check codex mcp list # remove codex plugin remove context-mode@context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
Gemini CLI ```sh gemini extensions install https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode ``` ```sh # update gemini extensions update context-mode # check GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true gemini mcp list # remove gemini extensions uninstall context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (package) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
Qwen Code ```sh qwen extensions install https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode:context-mode ``` ```sh # update qwen extensions update context-mode # check qwen extensions list # remove qwen extensions uninstall context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (package) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
Pi ```sh pi install npm:context-mode ``` ```sh # update pi update --extensions # check pi list # remove pi remove npm:context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (the plugin's own event handlers) · MCP ✓ (ctx tools built into the plugin) · Skills ✓
OpenCode ```sh opencode plugin add context-mode ``` ```sh # update opencode plugin update # check opencode mcp list --pure # OpenCode 1.19 opencode mcp list --standalone # OpenCode 2 # remove opencode plugin remove context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (the plugin's own event handlers) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
Copilot CLI ```sh npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup --agents copilot-cli ``` ```sh # update context-mode upgrade # check context-mode doctor --agents copilot-cli copilot mcp list # remove context-mode setup --remove --agents copilot-cli ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
Kiro ```sh npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup --agents kiro ``` ```sh # update context-mode upgrade # check context-mode doctor --agents kiro # remove context-mode setup --remove --agents kiro ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
VS Code (Copilot) ```sh npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup --agents vscode ``` ```sh # update context-mode upgrade # check context-mode doctor --agents vscode # remove context-mode setup --remove --agents vscode ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
ZCode ```sh zcode plugins marketplace add mksglu/context-mode zcode plugins install context-mode@context-mode ``` ```sh # update zcode plugins update context-mode@context-mode # check zcode plugins list # remove zcode plugins uninstall context-mode@context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
The npm route works for every agent: ```sh npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup ``` Setup is also the repair. It shows a plan, saves your earlier config, then applies the plan; when a step ends early, it restores the saved config. To uninstall: ```sh context-mode setup --remove npm rm -g context-mode ``` Restart the agent, then run `/ctx-doctor` in it. Each check prints PASS or a fix command, and the [Doctor guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/doctor?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install-doctor) explains each check.
How we tested the install Every agent gets hooks, the MCP server and the plugin skills; the last line of each block above says how. Hooks reach each agent in one of three ways: in the plugin package (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code), in a hook file (Codex, Copilot CLI, Kiro, VS Code, ZCode), or in a plugin inside the agent (OpenCode, Pi). The [Agents guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/agents?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install-agents) shows what each agent runs. We ran the real binary of each agent with the plugin hook: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Pi, OpenCode, Copilot CLI and ZCode. Each run used a clean temp home and a local test model, on 2.0.0-next.15. For VS Code and Kiro, the check covers the hook setup: VS Code runs the hook command with the documented payload, and kiro-cli 2.35.2 loads all 6 hook entries. CI runs setup, doctor, a hook and an MCP handshake for all 10 agents from the packed package on Linux, macOS and Windows. Record: [HOOKS-FIRE.md](docs/architecture/release/HOOKS-FIRE.md). Each agent uses its own install command, and [ADR-0023](docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0023-native-install.md) says why.
Your first task with the plugin, step by step: [First session](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/first-session?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install-next). Or paste a prompt from [Try it](#try-it) right now. ## Try it Paste one of these prompts into your agent after the install. Each one ran once, live, in Claude Code 2.1.312, and its answer matched the source data ([evidence and rerun steps](bench/evidence/try-it-2026-11-02/README.md)). The headline numbers in [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) use the median of 5 runs. Other agents do the same job with the same tools: `ctx_execute`, `ctx_index` and `ctx_search`. After a prompt, run the stats skill and read the report yourself ([See the saving](#see-the-saving)). ```text On https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffect, show me the example that connects to a chat server and cleans up, and list the rules for the dependency array. ``` The hook sends WebFetch to the sandbox, and the agent searches the page for the example and the rules. 601,984 B raw, 20,860 B reached the context, 96.5% saved (2026-11-02, 2.0.0-next.26, claude-haiku-5-5). ```text Fetch https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/photos. The agent reads files, runs the suite and fetches docs, and each result goes into the context window. When the window is full, the host compacts it, and from then on the agent sees a short summary plus your next message. Context Mode keeps the full output of each large tool call in `context.db` on your machine and gives the agent a small reply. At compaction, a snapshot of at most 2,048 B keeps the session state. After the compaction, the agent calls `ctx_resume` to read that snapshot back and `ctx_search` to find any earlier output by keyword. In the bench, a scripted session of 40 tool outputs and one compaction made a 442,893 B transcript, and the `ctx_resume` block that brought the agent back was 2,019 B (row `e-long-session` in the bench file; [open the case](bench/e-continuity/README.md#e-long-session)). In the same bench, one large log of 666,796 B put 3,380 B into the context, and the full log stayed in the index for `ctx_search` (row `d-synth-1m`; [open the case](bench/d-externalize/README.md#d-synth-1m)). How the snapshot picks what to keep: the [Long sessions guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/long-sessions?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=longer-sessions) and [ADR-0009](docs/architecture/adr/0009-compaction-and-memory.md). ### Speed Median of 5 runs, bench of 2026-11-01. | Measure | Result | |---|---| | Hook time over a bare `node` start, per agent | 7.5 ms to 12.3 ms | | `ctx_search`, 20 queries over 8 indexed files | 1.62 ms median, 6.70 ms max | | `ctx_index`, 3 real files, 625,649 B | 150 ms per MB | Source: rows `g-hook-kiro` to `g-hook-claude-code`, `g-search-latency` and `g-index-per-mb` of [the bench file](bench/results/2026-11-01-darwin-arm64.md), with every agent and query. Next, what happens inside one tool call, in [How it works](#how-it-works). ## How it works One tool call, in time order, from the install to a hook error. 1. **Install.** Each agent's own install command adds the MCP server, the hooks and the skills `ctx-doctor`, `ctx-stats` and `ctx-upgrade` to that agent's config folder, for example `~/.codex/skills//SKILL.md`. `context-mode setup` writes or repairs any part the native command leaves out ([ADR-0023](docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0023-native-install.md)). 2. **Session start.** The `SessionStart` hook opens the project database. When the session ran before, the agent gets one line that tells it to call `ctx_resume` ([dispatch.ts](src/core/hooks/dispatch.ts)). 3. **PreToolUse checks.** Before a tool runs, the `PreToolUse` hook checks the call in a fixed order: the user's deny list, WebFetch, curl and wget, inline HTTP and build commands, then a full-file Read over `OUTPUT_CAP` (16,384 B) and one-file shell dumps such as `cat` or `tail`. A Read with a line range runs as usual ([decide.ts](src/core/policy/decide.ts)). 4. **The exact call.** When a check matches, the hook stops the call and its reply names the exact `ctx_*` call to use, for example `ctx_execute` with `{"language":"shell","code":"","intent":""}`. For WebFetch the reply names `ctx_index`, then `ctx_search` ([read-deny.ts](src/core/policy/read-deny.ts)). 5. **The sandbox.** This is the Thinking in Code step: the agent's script runs here, and only what it prints comes back. `ctx_execute` writes the script to a temp folder and spawns the runtime from an argument list in the project folder. The timeout is `EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS` (600,000 ms, default and maximum); on timeout it stops the whole process group (`taskkill /F /T` on Windows). The child gets your environment minus preload variables such as `NODE_OPTIONS`, and the agent gets what the script prints, at most `OUTPUT_CAP` ([execute.ts](src/core/tools/execute.ts)). **Thinking in Code.** The agent sends a short script as a tool parameter, the script reads the data in the sandbox, and only what it prints goes into the context. Two real calls, in the form the Claude Code terminal shows them: `ctx_execute` on 5,000 JSON records, from the Claude Code 2.1.312 stream of the Try-it run with Context Mode 2.0.0-next.26 ([04-api-json.json](bench/evidence/try-it-2026-11-02/04-api-json.json)). The data is 1,039,898 B; the agent gets 254 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_execute (MCP)(language: "javascript", c…jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/photos\"); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(\"HTTP \" + res.status); const photos = await res.json(); let longest = null; for (const p of photos) { if (!longest || p.title.length > longest.title.length) longest = p; } const withEst = photos.filter(p => p.title.includes(\"est\")).length; const ties = photos.filter(p => p.title.length === longest.title.length).map(p => p.id); console.log(JSON.stringify({ total: photos.length, longest…nd count of titles containing \"est\"") ⎿ exit 0 · 239 B { "total": 5000, "longest": { "id": 653, "title": "temporibus commodi et fugit doloremque re…rit exercitationem necessitatibus aut", "length": 86 }, "longestTieIds": [ 653 ], "titlesContainingEst": 892 } ``` `ctx_batch` on an install log and a long git log, one live MCP call to `release-out/server.mjs` of Context Mode 2.0.0-next.36 on 2026-11-03 ([2026-11-03-ctx-batch.json](bench/evidence/thinking-in-code/2026-11-03-ctx-batch.json)). The commands print 228,881 B; the agent gets 8,667 B, the parts that match its two queries, and the full output stays in the index. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_batch (MCP)(commands: ["cat npm-install… queries: ["cache miss","feat commit"]) ⎿ ## cache miss js.org/@esbuild%2fwin32-x64 282ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2flinux-s390x 79ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2fopenbsd-x64 101ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2fwin32-arm64 99ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2fdarwin-arm64 99ms (cache miss) … +95 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` 6. **Indexing.** The full output goes into the index in chunks of at most `MAX_CHUNK_BYTES` (4,096 B). A Markdown chunk stays inside one heading section, and a code block that fits stays whole. Each chunk goes into two SQLite FTS5 tables: a Porter-stemmed table for words and a trigram table for paths, names and parts of words ([fts.ts](src/core/store/fts.ts)). `ctx_index` on a copy of this repo's `docs/how-it-works.md`, one live MCP call to `release-out/server.mjs` of Context Mode 2.0.0-next.36 on 2026-11-03 ([calls.json](bench/evidence/terminal-calls-2026-11-03/calls.json)). The file is 11,577 B; the agent gets 64 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_index (MCP)(path: "how-it-works.md") ⎿ Indexed 1 source(s), 17 chunk(s) from s1. Label: how-it-works.md ``` 7. **Search.** `ctx_search` ranks each table with BM25 and joins the two lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion: a hit scores 1/(`RRF_K` + rank), with `RRF_K` = 60. Before it returns an empty list, it tries a spelling fix from the indexed words. Search covers this session, this worktree (the default) or the whole project, and each snippet is at most `SNIPPET_MAX_BYTES` (800 B) ([search.ts](src/core/tools/search.ts)). `ctx_search` on that index, in the same run, in a project that also holds an `AGENTS.md`. One search reads the index and every agent's memory files. The agent gets 1,268 B: one content hit and one memory hit, each with its source and heading. For memory shared across machines, agents and sessions, see [Context Mode Gateway Memory](https://contextmode.ai/docs/memory?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=search-memory). ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_search (MCP)(queries: ["compaction state block"]) ⎿ Query "compaction state block": how-it-works.md #14: ### Session continuity The hooks log each prompt, edit, command, tool error, i…e same rows always give the same bytes. memory AGENTS.md #0: # Agent rules … +10 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` 8. **Run, then replace.** On hosts that run the tool first, the `PostToolUse` hook checks the result. Output over `REPLACE_TRIGGER_BYTES` (4,096 B) goes into the index whole, and the agent gets the best-matching chunks and one `ctx_search` line for the rest ([dispatch.ts](src/core/hooks/dispatch.ts)). 9. **Journal and compaction.** The hooks log each prompt, edit, command, tool error and decision in a journal. After a compaction the agent gets a state block of at most `STATE_BUDGET` (2,048 B), and each long line becomes a `ctx_resume(seq)` pointer to the full row; one `ctx_resume` reply is at most `RESUME_CAP` (2,048 B). On the next prompt, a prompt-match block brings back the journal rows that match it by BM25 ([ADR-0009](docs/architecture/adr/0009-compaction-and-memory.md)). `ctx_resume` with empty parameters returns the state block, in the same run: 209 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_resume (MCP)() ⎿ indexed how-it-works.md source s1: how-it-works.md (11536 B) more: ctx_search(queries:[], scope:"session") ``` 10. **The database.** Each project has one `context.db` under `~/.context-mode`, in Node's built-in `node:sqlite`. The database runs in WAL mode and runs a PASSIVE checkpoint on close. A new database gets built under a temp name and moves into place in one atomic step, and the busy timeout is `DB_TIMEOUT_MS` (5,000 ms) ([db.ts](src/core/store/db.ts)). 11. **A hook error.** A hook always ends with exit 0. On any error it gives the host's allow reply and writes one log line to `~/.context-mode/hook-errors.log`, so your agent keeps working. A spawned hook has `HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` (5,000 ms) ([fallback.ts](src/core/hooks/fallback.ts)). Every number with its reason: [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md). The rules the hook follows: [ADR-0008](docs/architecture/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md). Commands in the agent: `/ctx-stats` shows the `ctx_stats` result, `/ctx-doctor` runs `ctx_doctor` (send its report with a defect report), and `/ctx-upgrade` runs `ctx_upgrade`, then `ctx_doctor`. ## Security and privacy - The plugin keeps all its data on your machine, one database per project in `~/.context-mode`, and `ctx_purge` deletes it by session, source or project. Read the [Security guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/security?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=security). - The plugin has zero telemetry: usage data, events and crash reports stay on your machine. It uses the network for four calls, each one started by you or your agent: | Call | When | File | |---|---|---| | Fetch of a URL, for `ctx_index` | Your agent asks for a page. The fetch blocks private and link-local addresses, checks each address the host name points to, connects to the address it checked, and checks again at each redirect. | [fetch.ts](src/core/sandbox/fetch.ts) | | One read of the npm dist-tags, with `git ls-remote` of the release tags as the fallback | You run `context-mode doctor`, to check for a new version | [doctor-env.ts](src/core/ops/doctor-env.ts) | | `npm i -g context-mode`, or `gh issue create` | You run `context-mode upgrade`, or you press a key to send the debug report | [commands.ts](src/cli/commands.ts) | | Your agent's own install command, npm or git | You install or update | Your agent | - The guard test D-PRIVACY-NET-1 in [tests/0008-enforcement.test.mjs](tests/0008-enforcement.test.mjs) scans the source for HTTP clients, sockets, DNS lookups, git network calls and gh or npm spawns. It flags each new call site, so this table stays true. - Doctor and the debug report remove secrets by their structure before they print. Code from `ctx_execute` runs on your host as your user, with your files, your network and your environment except the preload variables, so keep your agent's own permission prompts on. Here "sandbox" means the output stays in the sandbox and out of the context. What the plugin stores, where, and how to delete it: [Privacy](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/privacy?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=privacy). ## Context Mode Gateway The plugin works on tool output, on your machine, and it is complete on its own. Context Mode Gateway is a separate hosted service with its own account and subscription. It works on every request, across all your agents. Its 11 features, the full list: Context Saving, Recall, Memory, Skills, Search, Session resume, Active Context, Instructions, Protect, Prompt caching, Live and Analytics. Add the Gateway when you want savings on every request, memory across sessions and agents, or cost reports for a team. For one project on one machine, the plugin covers the job. The two work together: [Gateway guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/gateway?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=gateway). Gateway Recall, Search and Session resume run on the Gateway server, across sessions and agents. The plugin's `ctx_search` and `ctx_resume` read the local `context.db` of one project. With the Gateway on, your requests pass through its server; the plugin keeps its own data on your machine. | Product | Runs | Scope | Billing | |---|---|---|---| | Context Mode plugin | On your machine | One project, local `context.db` | Free | | Context Mode Gateway | Hosted service | All sessions and agents | Subscription, separate from the plugin | Set up the Gateway with one command: ```sh npx @context-mode/cli ``` `npx @context-mode/cli` signs you in to your Gateway account, which has its own subscription, and writes one config change per agent. Apps: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Codex Desktop, T3 Code, OpenCode and Pi. Numbers in these screens come from the author's own account over 30 days (Oct 3 - Nov 1, 2026), so read them as one account's usage. Click an image for the full size. Three prompts to try with the Gateway on. The line under each one names the feature it shows. ```text Move this project from Jest to Vitest. Convert every test file, fix the config, run the suite after each batch, and tell me what is left. ``` Memory keeps the plan and the file list across a long job. ```text Pick up where we stopped yesterday on the Jest to Vitest move. What is done, what is left, and which test was failing? ``` Recall brings back yesterday's work in a fresh session. ```text Which date library did we choose on Tuesday, and why did we reject the other two? ``` Search finds the answer in past sessions.
Gateway features, from contextmode.ai/docs Source: [contextmode.ai/docs](https://contextmode.ai/docs/how-saving-works?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=features): | Feature | What it does | What you get | Details | |---|---|---|---| | Context Saving | Folds old tool output, runs data work as code (Thinking in Code), trims tool schemas, places cache marks | A tool output over 2,048 B becomes a short pointer, with the full copy archived | Saves the most on sessions with many tool calls | | Recall | The model sees recent work and an index of older work; the agent searches the archive for the rest | Gateway, Claude Code, Opus 5.5, 200K window, 2026-10-04: mean cost per session $4.8627 to $3.0353 (-37.6% in dollars, `ab.json` below) | Cost measured in Claude Code on Claude Opus 5.5 | | Memory | Each fact keeps two times: when it was true and when the Gateway learned it | Claude Code and Codex on one account share one store, tested end to end | The memory block goes into the first request of a new session | | Skills | A skill catalog on the Gateway for your account; it loads the skill that matches your message | The matching skill loads on the message that needs it | Import skills from GitHub; a loaded skill joins the prompt in full | | Search | Searches the prompts, commands and tool output that passed through, in the console and as an agent tool | Find any past prompt, command or tool output, from the console or your agent | The console searches the first 4,000 characters of each tool result | | Session resume | One command rebuilds a conversation as a native Claude Code or Codex session | Continue a conversation in Claude Code or Codex | Restores the text, tool names and a summary; the command is valid for 15 minutes | | Active Context | Sets how much a thread carries before its oldest parts move to the archive: 200K, 500K or 1M tokens | Pick the window size per thread | An image older than the kept part becomes a short text note | | Instructions | One text of at most 4,096 characters that tells every agent how to answer you | Read from the provider cache after the first request | Sets how the agent writes to you | | Protect | A tool-call firewall: checks shell commands, file reads and writes, web fetches and tool-server calls by what they do | Each call checked before it runs | Reads the call itself, so keep your agent's sandbox on for script files and paths built at run time; opt-in | | Prompt caching | Keeps requests cache-friendly: cache marks on the fixed part of the prompt and a cache for fetched pages | Inside the measured costs above | Uses up to 4 cache marks, the provider's maximum | | Live and Analytics | Shows each request and what the Gateway saved, as it happens and over time | See each request and its saving, live and over time | Covers every request that passes through the Gateway |
Gateway only: its cost against Claude Code alone, Claude Opus 5.5, mean dollars per session at list price. The plugin numbers are in [Benchmarks](#benchmarks). - Six short tasks (2026-09-29): 24.5% fewer dollars pooled over 176 sessions (21% to 29% per task). [v3-opus55-short.json](https://contextmode.ai/benchmarks/data/v3-opus55-short.json?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=bench) - Long Claude Code session, 200K window (2026-10-03/04): mean cost per session $4.8627 to $3.0353 (-37.6% in dollars, mean of 3 pairs). [ab.json](https://contextmode.ai/benchmarks/recall/200k-r2/ab.json?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=bench) - We fixed the rules before each run: [contextmode.ai/docs/benchmarks](https://contextmode.ai/docs/benchmarks?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=bench). The Gateway routes to Anthropic and OpenAI. The Gateway sends your requests to its server on the way to the model. It keeps a searchable record of your sessions for Recall and Search, and masks secrets and e-mail addresses when it reads archived output back. Its privacy page is at [contextmode.ai/privacy](https://contextmode.ai/privacy?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=privacy). Keep your agent's own sandbox on next to Protect. ## License Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2, the `LICENSE` file), a source-available license. You may use, copy, change and share the code, and use it at work, free of charge. The license keeps three uses for the licensor: 1. Offering the software to others as a hosted or managed service that gives them a large part of its features. 2. Moving, changing, turning off or getting around the license key functions, or removing or hiding what the license key protects. 3. Changing, removing or hiding the licensor's license, copyright or other notices. We chose ELv2 so the source stays open to all and the hosted service stays with the project. ## Community Report a defect on [Discord](https://discord.gg/DCN9jUgN5v) with the full `/ctx-doctor` report, and send ideas there too. The maintainer writes every change; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) shows how an agent files an issue. **Videos.** [Better Stack on Context Mode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QUHrntlfPo4). Make your own video and share it on [Discord](https://discord.gg/DCN9jUgN5v); we add videos over 10K views here.

repositories.name: dbdelve
repositories.description: Fast and lightweight DB Client made in Rust and GPUI.
repositories.readme: # DBDelve A fast, native, cross-platform, multi-engine database client. Written in Rust with GPUI, no Electron and no JVM: instant startup, friendly on your memory, and smooth scrolling through large tables where other clients crash or introduce limits. ## Community Ideas and discussion on [Discord](https://discord.gg/7PegWzwqCm). Like DBDelve? [Support its development](https://www.patreon.com/cw/ShayanAbbas1). Support is voluntary and does not provide any additional benefits. ![DBDelve in Gruvbox Dark Glass: a SELECT on the events table in the editor and its result grid below](assets/screenshots/query-dark.png) ![DBDelve in Gruvbox Light Glass: a join in the editor and its result grid below](assets/screenshots/query-light.png) Scrolling a million rows: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e15d566-a110-46c6-a236-52af7d877d4c Launching, with the last results already there: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e55da56-8577-43e0-812a-c77eb5d0e701 ## Why I wanted something which is performant, modern and consumes little ram. The existing DB clients are either filled with bloat (Electron and JVM) or paid. This is an alternative to them. No feature is ever going behind a paywall and with time we will have complete parity on features with those too. ## Install **macOS** (Apple Silicon, macOS 12 or later): ```sh brew install --cask ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/dbdelve ``` The app isn't notarized, so the cask clears the quarantine flag macOS would otherwise refuse it over. Without Homebrew: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/main/install.sh | sh ``` **Linux** (x86_64 or aarch64): the same one-liner installs it under `~/.local` with no root, or `yay -S dbdelve-bin` from the AUR, or the tarball or AppImage from [the latest release][releases]. **Windows** (x86_64): run the installer from [the latest release][releases], or unzip the zip and run `dbdelve.exe`. The installer asks for AppData (just for you) or Program Files (all users). Updating, the `.dmg`, Linux requirements, building from source and where your data lives are all in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md). [releases]: https://github.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/releases/latest ## Supported databases Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Turso, DuckDB, Snowflake, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis (and Valkey, KeyDB, Dragonfly) and ClickHouse. Any other database with an ODBC driver is reachable through the bundled ODBC bridge, with that driver installed: IBM Db2, Oracle, SAP HANA, SAP ASE (Sybase), Informix, Teradata, Vertica, Exasol, Firebird, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, Databricks, Apache Hive, Trino and Presto, Dremio, InterSystems IRIS, Microsoft Access and more. Grid editing is off, and statements you type run under the connection's mode. See [Connecting through ODBC](docs/odbc.md). ![The welcome screen: paste a connection URL or pick one of the engines, import from DBeaver or TablePlus, or pick a theme](assets/screenshots/welcome.png) ## What it does - **Make it yours.** The app's own themes alongside Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Gruvbox and Dracula, each in dark, light and glass. Import themes from Zed or VS Code, or [write your own](docs/themes.md). ![The theme picker, with themes imported from Zed and VS Code and the import commands below them](assets/screenshots/themes.png) - **Bring your connections with you.** Import every saved connection, passwords and SSH settings included, from DBeaver, or TablePlus on macOS. - **Organize your connections into projects,** and jump to any of them from the palette, or disconnect back to a home screen that lists them all. ![The palette scoped to connections, grouped into two projects, with the current connection marked](assets/screenshots/projects.png) - **Never mistake prod for staging.** Every connection is isolated and can color the title bar. Run it read-only, read-write or with full access, and DBDelve asks before anything destructive. ![The connection form, grouped into connection, security and behaviour, with a color and a project for the connection](assets/screenshots/connection-form.png) - **Edits you can read first.** Change a cell and DBDelve writes the `UPDATE` for you to check before it runs. - **Keep the columns you need.** Hide or pin columns, and the layout survives a restart. - **Read a row in full** in the row panel, with JSON highlighted, and edit long values there. ![A table open in the grid, with the row panel showing one row's values and its JSON highlighted](assets/screenshots/table-dark.png) - **Import rows** from CSV, TSV or JSON, with every row checked and every statement shown before anything runs. ![Importing events.csv: format options on the left, each file column mapped to a table column, and a preview of the rows](assets/screenshots/import.png) - **Open a data file** by dropping it on the window: a CSV, Excel, Parquet or JSON file opens in DuckDB, held in memory, as a query you can change. A `.sql` file opens in a new query tab on the connection you're on, and runs only when you run it. - **See the query plan** highlighted in its own pane, with bad row estimates called out. ![An Explain Analyze plan for a join: each node with its actual and estimated rows and time, and a ×76 misestimate flagged](assets/screenshots/query-plan.png) - **Completion that knows your schema:** tables, and a table's columns after its name and a dot. ![Completing accounts. to its columns in a join](assets/screenshots/completion.png) - **Keyboard-first.** One palette for commands, tables, saved queries, history and connections, and every shortcut rebindable. - **Your SSH, not a reimplementation.** Tunnels run through your own `ssh`, so your config, agent and hardware keys just work. For Postgres, a Host that is a directory (`/var/run/postgresql`) reaches that Unix socket on the SSH host, optionally as another user (Run as); the server needs `socat`, and passwordless `sudo` for it when Run as is set. TLS modes other than `disable` and `prefer` are refused there. - **Sign in with a short-lived token.** On Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Redis and ClickHouse, a profile's Password command prints the password at every login, so cloud IAM auth keeps working after the token expires. For Amazon RDS: ```sh /opt/homebrew/bin/aws rds generate-db-auth-token --hostname %HOSTNAME% --port %PORT% --username %USERNAME% --region ``` `%HOSTNAME%`, `%PORT%` and `%USERNAME%` are the profile's own. DBDelve quotes them itself, so write them unquoted: one inside quotes stops the command from running. Give the program's full path (`which aws` prints it): an app opened from the Finder or a desktop launcher does not see the PATH your shell sets. Expires after reuses the output for that many seconds, in memory only; blank runs the command at every login. Free and open source, nothing behind a paywall, and no telemetry: the only request DBDelve makes on its own is an update check, which you can turn off. ## Benchmarks DBDelve 0.3.6 against DBeaver 25.3.1 on the same Postgres table, median of 5 runs each (2026-10-11, M1 Pro, 32 GB): | | DBDelve | DBeaver | | ----------------- | ------- | ------- | | Launch | 1.1 s | 5.2 s | | Idle memory | 133 MB | 606 MB | | 1,000-row query | 0.21 s | 1.96 s | | 1M rows, time | 56 s | 208 s | | 1M rows, memory\* | 4.9 GB | 17 GB | \* The whole 1M-row table pulled into memory on purpose, with the row limit off. Method and full results in [BENCHMARKS.md](BENCHMARKS.md). ## Logs and bug reports DBDelve keeps a diagnostic log on your machine and never sends it anywhere. To attach it to an issue, use **Help → Copy Diagnostics** and paste; **Help → Open Logs Folder** shows the files. If the default log doesn't show the problem, turn on **Verbose logging** in Settings and reproduce it. Read a log before you post it and remove anything sensitive. A verbose one can hold hostnames, database names and anything a database driver logs. ## License Copyright (C) 2026 Shayan Abbas and contributors, licensed under the [GPL-3.0](LICENSE). Code contributed before the switch was released under the [MIT License](licenses/MIT-dbdelve.txt), and that notice still applies to it. Third-party font and theme licenses are in [NOTICES.md](NOTICES.md).

repositories.name: Pake
repositories.description: Turn any website into a lightweight desktop app with one command, on macOS, Windows and Linux.
repositories.readme:
Pake

Turn any website into a lightweight desktop app with one command. Supports macOS, Windows and Linux. Free open-source CLI, plus a desktop app.

English · 中文 · 繁體 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Deutsch · Français

> This repo is the free open-source Pake CLI, and everything below stays free. Prefer a graphical app? The Pake desktop app is a separate download from [pake.run](https://pake.run/), its only official site. It makes apps from a ready-made gallery or any URL without Node.js or Rust, with settings, updates and separate apps for other accounts in one window. `pnpm install -g pake-cli` installs the CLI only. ## Features - **Lightweight**: Installers are typically under 10 MB, nearly 20 times smaller than Electron packages, a lighter alternative to Nativefier and other Electron wrappers - **Fast**: Built with Rust Tauri on the system WebView instead of a bundled Chromium, so each app carries no browser engine of its own - **Easy to use**: One-command packaging via CLI or online building, no complex configuration needed - **Feature-rich**: Supports shortcuts, immersive windows, drag & drop, style customization, ad removal ## Getting Started - **Beginners**: Make apps without a command line in the [Pake desktop app](https://pake.run/), download ready-made [Popular Packages](#popular-packages) or use [Online Building](docs/github-actions-usage.md) with no environment setup required - **Developers**: Install [CLI Tool](docs/cli-usage.md) for one-command packaging of any website with customizable icons, window settings, and more - **Advanced Users**: Clone the project locally for [Custom Development](#development), or check [Advanced Usage](docs/advanced-usage.md) for style customization and feature enhancement - **Troubleshooting**: Check [FAQ](docs/faq.md) for common issues and solutions ## Popular Packages
WeRead Mac Windows Linux X Mac Windows Linux
Grok Mac Windows Linux DeepSeek Mac Windows Linux
ChatGPT Mac Windows Linux Gemini Mac Windows Linux
YouTube Music Mac Windows Linux YouTube Mac Windows Linux
LiZhi Mac Windows Linux ProgramMusic Mac Windows Linux
Excalidraw Mac Windows Linux XiaoHongShu Mac Windows Linux
Notion Mac Windows Linux Flomo Mac Windows Linux
More apps are on the [Releases](https://github.com/tw93/Pake/releases) page.
Keyboard shortcuts
| Mac | Windows/Linux | Function | | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | | ⌘ + [ | Ctrl + [ | Return to the previous page | | ⌘ + ] | Ctrl + ] | Go to the next page | | ⌘ + ↑ | Ctrl + ↑ | Auto scroll to top of page | | ⌘ + ↓ | Ctrl + ↓ | Auto scroll to bottom of page | | ⌘ + R | Ctrl + R | Refresh page | | ⌘ + W | Ctrl + W | Hide window, not quit | | ⌘ + - | Ctrl + - | Zoom out | | ⌘ + = | Ctrl + = | Zoom in | | ⌘ + 0 | Ctrl + 0 | Reset zoom | | ⌘ + L | Ctrl + L | Copy current page URL | | ⌘ + ⇧ + ⌥ + V | Ctrl + Shift + V | Paste and match style | | ⌘ + ⇧ + H | Ctrl + Shift + H | Go to home page | | ⌘ + ⌥ + I | Ctrl + Shift + I | Toggle developer tools (debug only) | | ⌘ + ⇧ + ⌫ | Ctrl + Shift + Del | Clear cache and restart | | ⌃ + ⌘ + F | F11 | Toggle native window fullscreen | Double-click the title bar to toggle fullscreen. On Windows and Linux, `--hide-window-decorations` gives a frameless window with a top drag region. On Mac, swipe to go back or forward and drag the title bar to move the window, and the menu bar has navigation, zoom and window controls.
## Command-Line Packaging ![Pake](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tw93/static/main/pake/pake1.gif) ```bash # Install Pake CLI pnpm install -g pake-cli # Basic usage, fetches the website icon automatically pake https://github.com --name GitHub # Advanced usage, custom options pake https://weekly.tw93.fun --name Weekly --icon https://cdn.tw93.fun/pake/weekly.icns --width 1200 --height 800 --hide-title-bar ``` The first build sets up the environment and takes a while, later builds are fast. See the [CLI Usage Guide](docs/cli-usage.md) for every option, or try [GitHub Actions Online Building](docs/github-actions-usage.md) if you'd rather skip the command line. Using Pake from a script or AI agent? Pass `--json` for machine-readable results, describe apps declaratively with `--config app.json` ([schema](schema/pake.schema.json)), and package local build output directly with `pake ./dist --name MyTool`. See [llms.txt](llms.txt) for the full agent contract. The official skill installs like this: ```text # Claude Code /plugin marketplace add tw93/Pake /plugin install pake@pake # Codex codex plugin marketplace add tw93/Pake codex plugin add pake@pake ``` Copy this to your AI agent to get started: ```text Use Pake (npm i -g pake-cli) to package webpages as desktop apps. Read https://unpkg.com/pake-cli@latest/llms.txt first; always run pake with --json and parse stdout as a single JSON object. Package into an app named . ``` ## Development Requires Rust `>=1.85` and Node `>=22` (recommended LTS; `>=20.9` also works), see the [Tauri documentation](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/) for setup. If you are new to this toolchain, the CLI is the easier path. ```bash # Install dependencies pnpm i # Local development, right-click to open the debug tools pnpm run dev # Build application pnpm run build ``` For style customization, feature enhancement, container communication and other advanced features, see [Advanced Usage Documentation](docs/advanced-usage.md). ## Contributors Pake wouldn't be possible without these incredible contributors. ## Support - Getting the [Pake desktop app](https://pake.run/) is the most direct way to support Pake's development - If Pake helped you, give it a star, [share it](https://x.com/intent/tweet?url=https://github.com/tw93/Pake&text=Pake%20-%20Turn%20any%20webpage%20into%20a%20desktop%20app%20with%20one%20command.%20Nearly%2020x%20smaller%20than%20Electron%20packages,%20supports%20macOS%20Windows%20Linux), or open an issue or PR, including sites that would make good desktop apps - I have two cats, TangYuan and Coke, and if Pake makes your life a little easier, feel free to treat them to canned food These lovely people already did ## License Pake is open source under GPL-3.0, see [LICENSE](./LICENSE) and [Pake Output Exception](./LICENSE-EXCEPTION); apps you build with Pake are entirely yours to use and distribute. If you fork Pake into your own product, to avoid confusion please give it a different name and credit Pake as the source. Pake CLI stays open source for the long run.

OBS Studio <https://obsproject.com>
===================================

.. image:: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/actions/workflows/push.yaml/badge.svg?branch=master
   :alt: OBS Studio Build Status - GitHub Actions
   :target: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/actions/workflows/push.yaml?query=branch%3Amaster

   :alt: OBS Studio Discord Server
   :target: https://obsproject.com/discord

What is OBS Studio?
-------------------

OBS Studio is software designed for capturing, compositing, encoding,
recording, and streaming video content, efficiently.

It's distributed under the GNU General Public License v2 (or any later
version) - see the accompanying COPYING file for more details.

Quick Links
-----------

- Website: https://obsproject.com

- Help/Documentation/Guides: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/wiki

- Forums: https://obsproject.com/forum/

- Build Instructions: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/wiki/Install-Instructions

- Developer/API Documentation: https://obsproject.com/docs

- Donating/backing/sponsoring: https://obsproject.com/contribute

- Bug Tracker: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/issues

Contributing
------------

- If you would like to help fund or sponsor the project, you can do so
  via `Patreon <https://www.patreon.com/obsproject>`_, `OpenCollective
  <https://opencollective.com/obsproject>`_, or `PayPal
  <https://www.paypal.me/obsproject>`_.  See our `contribute page
  <https://obsproject.com/contribute>`_ for more information.

- If you wish to contribute code to the project, please make sure to
  read the coding and commit guidelines:

- Code for the project follows the code style guidelines, located

- Other ways to contribute are by helping people out with support on
  our forums or in our community chat.  Please limit support to topics
  you fully understand -- bad advice is worse than no advice.  When it
  comes to something that you don't fully know or understand, please
  defer to the official help or official channels.

repositories.readme:
# Supabase [Supabase](https://supabase.com) is the Postgres development platform. We're building the features of Firebase using enterprise-grade open source tools. - [x] Hosted Postgres Database. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database) - [x] Authentication and Authorization. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth) - [x] Auto-generated APIs. - [x] REST. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api) - [x] GraphQL. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/graphql) - [x] Realtime subscriptions. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime) - [x] Functions. - [x] Database Functions. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/functions) - [x] Edge Functions. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions) - [x] File Storage. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage) - [x] AI + Vector/Embeddings Toolkit. [Docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai) - [x] Dashboard. ![Supabase Dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/supabase/master/apps/www/public/images/github/supabase-dashboard.png) Watch "releases" of this repo to get notified of major updates. ## Documentation For full documentation, visit [supabase.com/docs](https://supabase.com/docs) To see how to Contribute, visit [Getting Started](./DEVELOPERS.md) ## Community & Support - [Community Forum](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions). Best for: help with building, discussion about database best practices. - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues). Best for: bugs and errors you encounter using Supabase. - [Email Support](https://supabase.com/docs/support#business-support). Best for: problems with your database or infrastructure. - [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com). Best for: sharing your applications and hanging out with the community. ## How it works Supabase is a combination of open source tools. We’re building the features of Firebase using enterprise-grade, open source products. If the tools and communities exist, with an MIT, Apache 2, or equivalent open license, we will use and support that tool. If the tool doesn't exist, we build and open source it ourselves. Supabase is not a 1-to-1 mapping of Firebase. Our aim is to give developers a Firebase-like developer experience using open source tools. **Architecture** Supabase is a [hosted platform](https://supabase.com/dashboard). You can sign up and start using Supabase without installing anything. You can also [self-host](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/hosting/overview) and [develop locally](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development). ![Architecture](apps/docs/public/img/supabase-architecture.svg) - [Postgres](https://www.postgresql.org/) is an object-relational database system with over 30 years of active development that has earned it a strong reputation for reliability, feature robustness, and performance. - [Realtime](https://github.com/supabase/realtime) is an Elixir server that allows you to listen to PostgreSQL inserts, updates, and deletes using websockets. Realtime polls Postgres' built-in replication functionality for database changes, converts changes to JSON, then broadcasts the JSON over websockets to authorized clients. - [PostgREST](http://postgrest.org/) is a web server that turns your PostgreSQL database directly into a RESTful API. - [GoTrue](https://github.com/supabase/gotrue) is a JWT-based authentication API that simplifies user sign-ups, logins, and session management in your applications. - [Storage](https://github.com/supabase/storage-api) is a RESTful API for managing files in S3, with Postgres handling permissions. - [pg_graphql](http://github.com/supabase/pg_graphql/) is a PostgreSQL extension that exposes a GraphQL API. - [postgres-meta](https://github.com/supabase/postgres-meta) is a RESTful API for managing your Postgres, allowing you to fetch tables, add roles, and run queries, etc. - [Envoy](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy) is a cloud-native, high-performance edge and service proxy. #### Client libraries Our approach for client libraries is modular. Each sub-library is a standalone implementation for a single external system. This is one of the ways we support existing tools.

repositories.description: Cross-platform Xcode replacement. Build and deploy iOS apps with SwiftPM on Linux, Windows, macOS.
repositories.readme:
# xtool

Cross-platform Xcode replacement. Build and deploy iOS apps with SwiftPM on Linux, Windows, and macOS.

## Overview

xtool is a cross-platform (Linux/WSL/macOS) tool that replicates Xcode functionality with open standards.

✅ Build a SwiftPM package into an iOS app

✅ Sign and install iOS apps

✅ Interact with Apple Developer Services programmatically

## Getting Started

1. Follow the guide to install `xtool`
    - [Installation (Linux/Windows)](https://xtool.sh/documentation/xtooldocs/installation-linux)
    - [Installation (macOS)](https://xtool.sh/documentation/xtooldocs/installation-macos)
2. Create and run your first xtool-powered app by following the [tutorial](https://xtool.sh/tutorials/xtooldocs/first-app)!

## Examples

### Screenshot

![A screenshot of xtool being invoked from VSCode](Documentation/xtool.docc/Resources/Cover.png)

### Command line interface

```bash
$ xtool --help
OVERVIEW: Cross-platform Xcode replacement

USAGE: xtool <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  -h, --help              Show help information.

CONFIGURATION SUBCOMMANDS:
  setup                   Set up xtool for iOS development
  auth                    Manage Apple Developer Services authentication
  sdk                     Manage the Darwin Swift SDK

DEVELOPMENT SUBCOMMANDS:
  new                     Create a new xtool SwiftPM project
  dev                     Build and run an xtool SwiftPM project
  ds                      Interact with Apple Developer Services

DEVICE SUBCOMMANDS:
  devices                 List devices
  install                 Install an ipa file to your device
  uninstall               Uninstall an installed app
  launch                  Launch an installed app

  See 'xtool help <subcommand>' for detailed help.
```

### Library

You can consume xtool itself as a Swift Package, to enable your own app to interact with Apple Developer Services, iOS devices, and more. You can use this by adding `XKit` or `XToolSupport` as a SwiftPM dependency.

Note: while we aim to uphold semver semantics on the CLI interface (breaking change = major version bump), the Swift interface does not offer the same guarantees.

```swift
// package dependency:
.package(url: "https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool", .upToNextMinor(from: "1.2.0"))
// target dependency:
.product(name: "XKit", package: "xtool")
```

repositories.readme:
# uv An extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.

Installing Trio's dependencies with a warm cache.

## Highlights - A single tool to replace `pip`, `pip-tools`, `pipx`, `poetry`, `pyenv`, `twine`, `virtualenv`, and more. - [10-100x faster](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md) than `pip`. - Provides [comprehensive project management](#projects), with a [universal lockfile](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/layout#the-lockfile). - [Runs scripts](#scripts), with support for [inline dependency metadata](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/scripts#declaring-script-dependencies). - [Installs and manages](#python-versions) Python versions. - [Runs and installs](#tools) tools published as Python packages. - Includes a [pip-compatible interface](#the-pip-interface) for a performance boost with a familiar CLI. - Supports Cargo-style [workspaces](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces) for scalable projects. - Disk-space efficient, with a [global cache](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/cache) for dependency deduplication. - Installable without Rust or Python via `curl` or `pip`. - Supports macOS, Linux, and Windows. uv is backed by [Astral](https://astral.sh), the creators of [Ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) and [ty](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty). ## Installation Install uv with our standalone installers: ```bash # On macOS and Linux. curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh ``` ```bash # On Windows. powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex" ``` Or, from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/uv/): ```bash # With pip. pip install uv ``` ```bash # Or pipx. pipx install uv ``` If installed via the standalone installer, uv can update itself to the latest version: ```bash uv self update ``` See the [installation documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) for details and alternative installation methods. ## Documentation uv's documentation is available at [docs.astral.sh/uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv). Additionally, the command line reference documentation can be viewed with `uv help`. ## Features ### Projects uv manages project dependencies and environments, with support for lockfiles, workspaces, and more, similar to `rye` or `poetry`: ```console $ uv init example Initialized project `example` at `/home/user/example` $ cd example $ uv add ruff Creating virtual environment at: .venv Resolved 2 packages in 170ms Built example @ file:///home/user/example Prepared 2 packages in 627ms Installed 2 packages in 1ms + example==0.1.0 (from file:///home/user/example) + ruff==0.5.0 $ uv run ruff check All checks passed! $ uv lock Resolved 2 packages in 0.33ms $ uv sync Resolved 2 packages in 0.70ms Checked 1 package in 0.02ms ``` See the [project documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/) to get started. uv also supports building and publishing projects, even if they're not managed with uv. See the [publish guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/publish/) to learn more. ### Scripts uv manages dependencies and environments for single-file scripts. Create a new script and add inline metadata declaring its dependencies: ```console $ echo 'import requests; print(requests.get("https://astral.sh"))' > example.py $ uv add --script example.py requests Updated `example.py` ``` Then, run the script in an isolated virtual environment: ```console $ uv run example.py Reading inline script metadata from: example.py Installed 5 packages in 12ms ``` See the [scripts documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/scripts/) to get started. ### Tools uv executes and installs command-line tools provided by Python packages, similar to `pipx`. Run a tool in an ephemeral environment using `uvx` (an alias for `uv tool run`): ```console $ uvx pycowsay 'hello world!' Resolved 1 package in 167ms Installed 1 package in 9ms + pycowsay==0.0.0.2 """ ------------ < hello world! > ------------ \ ^__^ \ (oo)\_______ (__)\ )\/\ ||----w | || || ``` Install a tool with `uv tool install`: ```console $ uv tool install ruff Resolved 1 package in 6ms Installed 1 package in 2ms + ruff==0.5.0 Installed 1 executable: ruff $ ruff --version ruff 0.5.0 ``` See the [tools documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/tools/) to get started. ### Python versions uv installs Python and allows quickly switching between versions. Install multiple Python versions: ```console $ uv python install 3.12 3.13 3.14 Installed 3 versions in 972ms + cpython-3.12.12-macos-aarch64-none (python3.12) + cpython-3.13.9-macos-aarch64-none (python3.13) + cpython-3.14.0-macos-aarch64-none (python3.14) ``` Download Python versions as needed: ```console $ uv venv --python 3.12.0 Using Python 3.12.0 Creating virtual environment at: .venv Activate with: source .venv/bin/activate $ uv run --python pypy@3.8 -- python --version Python 3.8.16 (a9dbdca6fc3286b0addd2240f11d97d8e8de187a, Dec 29 2022, 11:45:30) [PyPy 7.3.11 with GCC Apple LLVM 13.1.6 (clang-1316.0.21.2.5)] on darwin Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information. >>>> ``` Use a specific Python version in the current directory: ```console $ uv python pin 3.11 Pinned `.python-version` to `3.11` ``` See the [Python installation documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/install-python/) to get started. ### The pip interface uv provides a drop-in replacement for common `pip`, `pip-tools`, and `virtualenv` commands. uv extends their interfaces with advanced features, such as dependency version overrides, platform-independent resolutions, reproducible resolutions, alternative resolution strategies, and more. Migrate to uv without changing your existing workflows — and experience a 10-100x speedup — with the `uv pip` interface. Compile requirements into a platform-independent requirements file: ```console $ uv pip compile requirements.in \ --universal \ --output-file requirements.txt Resolved 43 packages in 12ms ``` Create a virtual environment: ```console $ uv venv Using Python 3.12.3 Creating virtual environment at: .venv Activate with: source .venv/bin/activate ``` Install the locked requirements: ```console $ uv pip sync requirements.txt Resolved 43 packages in 11ms Installed 43 packages in 208ms + babel==2.15.0 + black==24.4.2 + certifi==2024.7.4 ... ``` See the [pip interface documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/pip/index/) to get started. ## Contributing We are passionate about supporting contributors of all levels of experience and would love to see you get involved in the project. See the [contributing guide](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv?tab=contributing-ov-file#contributing) to get started. ## FAQ #### How do you pronounce uv? It's pronounced as "you - vee" ([`/juː viː/`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English#Key)) #### How should I stylize uv? Just "uv", please. See the [style guide](./STYLE.md#styling-uv) for details. #### What platforms does uv support? See uv's [platform support](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/platforms/) document. #### Is uv ready for production? Yes, uv is stable and widely used in production. See uv's [versioning policy](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/versioning/) document for details. ## Acknowledgements uv's dependency resolver uses [PubGrub](https://github.com/pubgrub-rs/pubgrub) under the hood. We're grateful to the PubGrub maintainers, especially [Jacob Finkelman](https://github.com/Eh2406), for their support. uv's Git implementation is based on [Cargo](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo). Some of uv's optimizations are inspired by the great work we've seen in [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/), [Orogene](https://github.com/orogene/orogene), and [Bun](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun). We've also learned a lot from Nathaniel J. Smith's [Posy](https://github.com/njsmith/posy) and adapted its [trampoline](https://github.com/njsmith/posy/tree/main/src/trampolines/windows-trampolines/posy-trampoline) for Windows support. ## License uv is licensed under either of - Apache License, Version 2.0, ([LICENSE-APACHE](LICENSE-APACHE) or ) - MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](LICENSE-MIT) or ) at your option. Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in uv by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dually licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

## 🔌 See the leading Postiz features

## ✨ Features | ![Image 1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a27ee220-beb7-4c7e-8c1b-2c44301f82ef) | ![Image 2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb5f5f15-ed90-47fc-811c-03ccba6fa8a2) | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | ![Image 3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d51786ee-ddd8-4ef8-8138-5192e9cfe7c3) | ![Image 4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91f83c89-22f6-43d6-b7aa-d2d3378289fb) | ### Our Sponsors | Sponsor | Logo | Description | |---------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------:|-----------------| | [Hostinger](https://www.hostinger.com/vps/docker/postiz?ref=postiz) | | Hostinger is on a mission to make online success possible for anyone – from developers to aspiring bloggers and business owners | | [Virlo](https://dev.virlo.ai/?ref=postiz) | | Virlo is the #1 social media trend spotting and all-in-one GTM tool for teams leveraging short-form video | | [ChatbotX](https://chatbotx.io/?ref=postiz) | | The ManyChat alternative that you can self-host, white-label, and resell to your clients. Bring your own OpenClaw, Hermes, or Claude agents! | | [RapidProxy](https://www.rapidproxy.io/?ref=postiz) | | RapidProxy provides 90M+ residential IPs for social media, browser automation, and AI workflows, with smart rotation and stable sessions. From $0.55/GB; use RAPID10 for 10% off. # Intro - Schedule all your social media posts (many AI features) - Measure your work with analytics. - Collaborate with other team members to exchange or buy posts. - Invite your team members to collaborate, comment, and schedule posts. - Perfect for automation (API) with platforms like N8N, Make.com, Zapier, etc. ## Tech Stack - Pnpm workspaces (Monorepo) - NextJS (React) - NestJS - Prisma (Default to PostgreSQL) - Temporal - Resend (email notifications) ## Quick Start To have the project up and running, please follow the [Quick Start Guide](https://docs.postiz.com/quickstart) ## Sponsor Postiz We now offer a few options to sponsor Postiz: - Just a donation: You like what we are building, and want to buy us some coffee so we can build faster. - Main repository: Get your logo with a backlink from the main Postiz repository. Postiz has over 7M downloads and 20k views per month. Link: https://opencollective.com/postiz

## Postiz Cloud vs. Open-source Choose [Postiz Cloud](https://postiz.com/) for a fully managed experience, or deploy Postiz Open-source on your own infrastructure. Both provide the same core Postiz product and features. We do not "gate" features or limit the license. The main difference is the infrastructure you need to own, approval from social media providers, and deployment that might be hard at times (let your LLM deploy it) | Area | Postiz Cloud | Postiz Open-source (self-hosted) | |---|---|---| | **Cost** | Subscription per plan, 7-day free trial | Free forever (AGPL-3.0); you pay only for your own infra | | **Setup time** | Sign up and connect channels in minutes | Deploy with Docker / Coolify / Railway / any VPS; you configure Postgres, Redis, storage and env vars | | **Hosting & data** | Hosted by Postiz; data stored in our infrastructure | Runs on your own server; data never leaves your environment | | **Social platform apps** | Pre-approved apps for every channel, ready to use | You create your own developer apps on each platform and go through their approval (Meta, YouTube, TikTok can take weeks) | | **Channels** | Limited by plan tier | Unlimited, every supported provider | | **Posts per month** | Limited by plan tier | Unlimited | | **Team members** | Limited by plan tier | Unlimited | | **Scheduling, calendar views, cross-posting, repeated posts, post comments & delays, sets, signatures** | Included | Included | | **Internal & Global Plugs, RSS auto-post, customer groups** | Included per plan | Included | | **Analytics** | Included per plan | Included (requires your own app credentials with analytics scopes) | | **AI Copilot, AI images, AI videos** | Included with monthly quotas per plan; keys managed by Postiz | Available if you bring your own OpenAI (and other provider) API keys; no quota, you pay the provider | | **AI video clipping** | Included with monthly clipping minutes per plan | Requires your own provider keys and extra configuration | | **Smart Agent** | Included per plan | Available with your own LLM key | | **Public API & webhooks** | Included per plan | Included | | **Agentic surfaces (MCP, CLI, Claude / ChatGPT / Codex / OpenClaw / Cursor connectors)** | Included, hosted MCP endpoint | Included, you point the MCP / CLI at your own instance | | **Custom integrations** | Included per plan | Included; you can also modify the code and add providers | | **Updates & maintenance** | Automatic, zero downtime for you | You pull new images and run migrations yourself | | **Uptime, backups, security patches** | Managed by Postiz | Your responsibility | | **Support** | Priority support via Discord / email per plan | Community support on Discord and GitHub | | **Source access & customization** | No (SaaS) | Full source code, fork and modify freely under AGPL | | **Compliance / data residency** | Postiz-controlled regions | Any region or air-gapped environment you choose |

## Postiz Compliance - This GitHub repository contains the open-source, self-hosted edition of Postiz. Postiz is also available as Postiz Cloud, a fully managed service at postiz.com. - Postiz hosted service uses official, platform-approved OAuth flows. - Postiz does not automate or scrape content from social media platforms. - Postiz does not collect, store, or proxy API keys or access tokens from users. - Postiz never asks users to paste API keys into our hosted product. - Postiz users always authenticate directly with the social platform (e.g., X, Discord, etc.), ensuring platform compliance and data privacy. ## License This repository's source code is available under the [AGPL-3.0 license](LICENSE).
